mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening, both of which tend to reduce equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by >1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by >1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals strong labor market expansion, which historically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening and is associated with lower equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% MoM for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the trajectory of real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a month-over-month increase in RSAFS predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) over any 5-year rolling window.
